score.moat_justification: Moderate/narrow moat built on scale and sourcing, not on pricing power over a proprietary asset: ARCC is the largest publicly traded BDC ($31.2B total assets at FY2025, 10-K Item 1) and sits inside the Ares Credit Group origination platform, which gives it first-look deal flow, sponsor relationships and underwriting infrastructure a sub-scale BDC cannot replicate, plus investment-grade access to cheap unsecured debt (debt/equity 1.12x at FY2025). The measured return history does not support a higher score: fundamentals.json ROE was 13.59% (FY2023), 11.40% (FY2024) and 9.07% (FY2025) — around, and falling toward, the cost of capital — and the roic_proxy series is null for this filer (no operating-income / invested-capital presentation for an investment company), as is any gross-margin series (a BDC presents total investment income and expenses, not COGS), so no ROIC or gross-margin claim is made. Against the moat: the underlying product (senior loans to sponsor-backed middle-market companies) is commoditized and contested by BXSL, Blue Owl, Apollo and bank re-entry, with spread compression compressing NII; the franchise is rented, not owned — ARCC is externally managed and pays base and incentive fees to Ares Capital Management; and leverage plus PIK income (a material share of investment income) mean credit losses in a downturn hit NAV directly. A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.

base_override.reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (BDC / investment company): the engine's OCF-based conservative OE is rejected as the base — for an investment company, purchases and sales of loans are operating cash flows, so OCF measures portfolio deployment, not earnings: FY2025 OCF was -$1,717M against net income of +$1,299M, and the OCF-based OE/share was negative in 4 of the last 5 fiscal years (only 1/5 OE-positive years in dcf_numbers.json) for a company that paid a covered $1.92/share dividend in each of those years (net investment income $1,415M / $2.02 per share in FY2025 per the 10-K statements of operations). The result would be a mechanical Tier F. For a BDC, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy (the FUTU/LPLA/WSE broker/payments precedent in this sweep): investment income and all expenses including adviser fees and interest are already in it, capex and SBC are filing-proven $0 (see the two overrides), and realized/unrealized gains and losses are a real, if volatile, part of a lender's total return. The median-of-3-FY normalization mirrors the engine's own base method applied to that definition. Declared under bounded authority (c): every input is a figure printed by this run's engine outputs.
base_override.source: Median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, built exclusively from this run's financials_history.csv (engine-filed figures): FY2023 net income $1,522,000,000 / 575,000,000 diluted shares = $2.6470; FY2024 $1,522,000,000 / 624,000,000 = $2.4391; FY2025 $1,299,000,000 / 699,000,000 = $1.8584; median of the three = $2.4391 (the FY2024 value).

# ARCC — Ares Capital Corp
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-17. Price $18.72 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap est. $13.09B — in scope under $40B. **Finance sector model misfit: read the base-override section before quoting any number from this file.**

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, fundamentals.json, statements.json, or the cited filing/press-release figures — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Closed-end, non-diversified management investment company regulated as a business development company (BDC), founded 2004 and externally managed by Ares Capital Management LLC (Ares Management subsidiary). At FY2025 it was the largest publicly traded BDC by market capitalization, with $31,235M of total assets and a $29,485M investment portfolio at fair value (FY2025 10-K / Q4 2025 release). It lends primarily first-lien senior secured loans to US middle-market (mostly sponsor-backed) companies. As a BDC/RIC it must distribute the bulk of taxable income: dividend declared $1.92/share in FY2025, FY2024 and FY2023 (fundamentals.json dps_declared), paid $1,264M in FY2025.

## Owner's earnings — both engine definitions rejected, and why
**Conservative (OCF − capex − SBC), from financials_history.csv:** FY2025 OCF −$1,717,000,000, capex $0 and SBC $0 by filing override (see OVERRIDES) → OE −$1,717,000,000 = **−$2.4564/share**. The maintenance definition prints the identical figure every year (oe_maintenance = oe_conservative in the CSV: no usable D&A or ΔNWC series is filed), so the two definitions collapse to one here. OE/share history: 2020 −$1.3679, 2021 −$5.5135, 2022 −$2.6236, 2023 +$0.8887, 2024 −$3.4103, 2025 −$2.4564 — positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years (dcf_numbers.json).

That series is a sector artifact, not an earnings record. For an investment company, buying and selling loans **is** the operating activity: the FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement runs "Purchases of investments" of $(14,075)M and "Proceeds from sales and repayments of investments and other transactions" of $11,216M through OPERATING ACTIVITIES. OCF is therefore negative in every year the portfolio grows, for a company whose FY2025 net investment income was $1,415.0M ($2.02/share, 10-K statements of operations) against a $1.92/share declared dividend, and whose GAAP net income was +$1,299,000,000 (filed EPS diluted $1.86).

**TTM check (ttm.py, ttm.json):** OCF FY −$1,717,000,000 − prior YTD −$517,000,000 + current YTD $520,000,000 = TTM −$680,000,000; capex $0 and SBC $0 (all three legs filled by the overrides); shares 718,000,000 → TTM OE −$680,000,000 = **−$0.9471/share**. Same artifact (H1 2026 was a net-deployment half), so the TTM pin is also rejected as a base. For reference, TTM net income through Q2 2026 was $960,000,000 (fundamentals.json) vs $1,299,000,000 in FY2025 — the earnings trend into 2026 is down, driven by unrealized losses (Q1 2026 GAAP EPS $0.13, Q2 2026 $0.24, company releases).

**Base used = median of the last 3 fiscal years' net income per diluted share, $2.4391/share** (base_override in judgment.json, bounded authority (c) — construction from this run's financials_history.csv only): FY2023 $1,522,000,000 / 575,000,000 = $2.6470; FY2024 $1,522,000,000 / 624,000,000 = $2.4391; FY2025 $1,299,000,000 / 699,000,000 = $1.8584; median $2.4391. Rationale (FUTU/LPLA/WSE precedent): for a lender, net income is the honest owner's-earnings proxy — investment income, adviser fees and interest expense are already in it, capex and SBC are filing-proven $0, and realized/unrealized gains and losses are a real part of a lender's total return. The median normalization mirrors the engine's own base method. Cross-check: the base sits above the current run rate (FY2025 NII $2.02/share; Q2 2026 core EPS $0.47/quarter) — that is deliberate normalization across the 2023–24 unrealized-gain years, and it is paid for with a 45% combined bear-or-worse probability weight and a flat base-case growth start. The method range is documented under Thoughts.

## OVERRIDES — capex $0 and SBC $0 (filing-proven), plus the base override
- **The gaps:** the preliminary engine run exited 4 with `DATA_GAP: sbc, capex` — no tier. Neither field has a filed value under any engine candidate tag in any year of companyfacts.
- **Capex $0 (kind "filing"):** the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-04, accession 0001287750-26-000006) Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows contains **no investing-activities section at all** — only OPERATING and FINANCING sections — and no purchases-of-property-and-equipment line. Its FY2025 totals reconcile exactly with no investing section: operating $(1,717)M + financing $1,781M = the reported $64M change in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash (beginning $860M, ending $924M), with no FX line. The same reconciliation holds in this run's statements.json (−1,717,000,000 + 1,781,000,000 = 64,000,000). ARCC's cash deployment is loan purchases, which are operating; it owns no operating PP&E base (ppe_net is blank in the engine history). This is the CMPS-style $0 proof: the amount is $0, not undisclosed.
- **SBC $0 (kind "filing"):** ARCC is externally managed and has no employees of its own; the adviser bears personnel compensation and ARCC pays base and incentive management fees instead (already expensed in net income). The 10-K contains no share-based/stock-based compensation line or adjustment in the cash-flow statement, no equity-incentive or stock-compensation note, and Note 9 (Stockholders' Equity) reports stock issued only by sale (ATM offerings: 42.4M shares, $937.2M gross proceeds in 2025) and, in 2024, on conversion of the 2024 convertible notes — no grants to anyone, including non-employee directors.
- **Out-of-band acknowledgments:** both overrides carry an `ack_reason` — with no filed value to band against, any value flags out-of-band mechanically (override_checks in dcf_numbers.json: out_of_band true, ack_reason_present true for both). These are filing-proven zeros, not estimates.
- **Measured impact (dcf_numbers.json override_impact):** on the engine-native OCF base the $0 fills change nothing arithmetically (base OE/share −$2.4564 with and without) and no weighted IRR exists on either side (negative base) — their effect is binary: without them there is no tier at all (`unblocks_tier`), and they are what let ttm.py compute at all. The base override's effect is the whole verdict: it replaces the rejected −$2.4564/share OCF base with the $2.4391/share net-income base declared above. On the TTM basis that score.json's override_impact measures, the combined override package moves the base from −$0.9471/share (the ttm.json OCF figure) to $2.4391/share, with weighted IRR — (no tier without) → 14.46%.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
Justification: scale and sourcing, not pricing power over a proprietary asset. The measured return history caps the score: fundamentals.json ROE was 13.59% (FY2023), 11.40% (FY2024), 9.07% (FY2025) — around, and falling toward, the cost of capital. The `roic_proxy` series is null for this filer (an investment company presents no operating-income / invested-capital split the proxy can use) and no gross-margin series exists (a BDC presents total investment income and expenses, not COGS), so no ROIC or gross-margin claim is made.
- FOR: largest publicly traded BDC by market cap ($31.2B total assets, FY2025 10-K) — scale in origination, diversification across hundreds of portfolio companies, and funding access; Ares Credit Group platform — sponsor relationships and direct-lending origination/underwriting infrastructure built since the 2004 IPO, with exited investments generating ~13% asset-level gross IRR since inception (company reporting); cheap termed-out funding — investment-grade unsecured access, debt/equity 1.12x at FY2025 within the 0.9–1.25x target range, weighted average stated interest on debt 4.8–4.9% (Q2 2026 presentation); dividend durability — $0.48/quarter declared continuously with a taxable spillover buffer (~$1.38/share per Q2 2026 coverage) covering multiple quarters of payout; credit record — non-accruals 2.4% at cost / 1.4% at fair value at Q2 2026, below the ~4% BDC historical average.
- AGAINST: the product is commoditized credit — senior middle-market loans are replicable by BXSL, Blue Owl, Apollo, other BDCs and returning banks, and spread compression flows straight into NII/share; the franchise is rented, not owned — externally managed, with base and incentive fees paid to Ares Capital Management; measured returns are ordinary and falling (ROE above; NAV/share $19.94 at FY2025 → $19.35 at Q2 2026); leverage (1.12–1.15x debt/equity) amplifies credit losses, and PIK interest/dividends were ~15% of Q2 2026 total investment income (company release coverage) — earnings quality below the headline; per-share growth is bought with issuance — share count +10.5%/yr via ATM offerings, and NII/share fell from $2.30 (FY2024) to $2.02 (FY2025) on the company's reported figures.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-17)
**Growth sanity check (mandatory):** the engine's blended growth is a 3.00% fallback default, not a measurement — every growth component is null because the engine maps no revenue tag for a BDC (the filer's total investment income, $3,052.0M in FY2025 per the 10-K statements of operations, is not an engine candidate tag). Recent per-share prints are flat-to-down: filed EPS diluted $2.68 → $2.44 → $1.86 (FY2023–25, statements.json), NII/share $2.30 → $2.02 (FY2024–25, company reporting), Q2 2026 core EPS $0.47 vs the $0.48 dividend, NAV/share falling. Scenario starts were therefore set against the per-share prints, via offsets −0.13 / −0.07 / −0.03 / +0.02 / +0.07 vs the 3% default, to −10 / −4 / **0** / +5 / +10%: the base case is *flat* per-share earnings — total portfolio growth (+10.3% in investments at fair value in FY2025) does not count, because it is funded by share issuance and has not produced per-share growth. Probabilities adjusted from the 10/25/30/25/10 default to **15/30/30/15/10** (45% bear-or-worse) for the falling per-share trend and the sector misfit. OE multipliers are the defaults (0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25). Price $18.72.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −10.0% | 0.75 | Credit cycle hits the loan book; realized losses and NAV erosion compound | $8.88 | 7.86% |
| Bear | 30% | −4.0% | 0.90 | Spread compression + soft exits grind NII/share down | $13.72 | 11.46% |
| Base | 30% | 0.0% | 1.00 | Per-share earnings stay flat at the normalized base; dividend covered, NAV roughly held | $18.02 | 14.52% |
| Bull | 15% | +5.0% | 1.10 | Spreads stabilize, deployment at accretive yields, core EPS back above the dividend | $24.41 | 18.68% |
| Super bull | 10% | +10.0% | 1.25 | Full private-credit upcycle with realized gains on top | $34.11 | 24.24% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $17.93 (−4.2% vs price), IV@12% $23.49, IV@10% $29.67, weighted IRR 14.46%, base-case IRR 14.52%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Hurdle prices (dcf_numbers.json): clears 20% only at or below $12.88, 25% only at or below $10.06. Diagnostics: OE yield 13.03%, terminal value 17.43% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.84x, 9.5 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc / DATA_GAP:capex** (preliminary run): resolved by the filing-proven $0 overrides — see OVERRIDES. The final run's data_gap_uncovered is empty.
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended ~10 months ago): ttm.py was run (ttm.json quoted above) — its OCF-based TTM OE is the same sector artifact and is not used as the base; the current-period evidence it and fundamentals.json carry (TTM net income $960,000,000 through Q2 2026 vs $1,299,000,000 in FY2025; Q2 2026 core EPS $0.47, NAV/share $19.35) is reflected in the flat base growth start and the 45% bear-or-worse weight.
- **DILUTION** (share count +10.5%/yr): this is ATM issuance funding portfolio growth ($928,000,000 of stock issued in FY2025, statements.json; $937.2M gross ATM proceeds per Note 9), not SBC dilution — SBC is filing-proven $0. It is handled where it actually bites: scenario growth is set on *per-share* prints (flat base), so issuance-funded book growth is never counted as per-share growth. Note the engine's −5pp share-count adjustment applies only to revenue blend components, which are all null here, so no adjustment entered the (default) blend.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024, 2025): structural, not a one-off — purchases of investments $(14,075)M vs proceeds $11,216M running through operating activities (FY2025 10-K) means net portfolio deployment, not an earnings/cash mismatch, drives the gap every year. Resolved by rejecting the OCF base (see Owner's earnings).
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): accepted — confidence is low, score.json records model_fit "misfit", and the ranking lists the name with the sector misfits. The verdict leans on the cross-checks a BDC is actually priced on: dividend coverage by NII ($2.02 vs $1.92 declared, FY2025) and NAV ($19.35/share at Q2 2026 vs the $18.72 price — the market is pricing ARCC at a small discount to NAV, not at an earnings multiple).
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: see OVERRIDES — gap, proof, out-of-band acknowledgments and measured impact are all recorded in judgment.json, dcf_numbers.json (overrides_applied / override_impact) and the registry.
- **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (net debt 9.0x normalized OE): the ratio divides by the rejected negative OCF base and is a template artifact. The balance sheet stated from the filing: total debt $15,991,000,000 (LongTermDebt total tag, FY2025) against stockholders' equity $14,318,000,000 — debt/equity 1.12x (statements.json metrics: 1.1168) — funding a $29,485M portfolio at fair value inside $31,235M of total assets. For a BDC, debt is the raw-material funding, and 1.12x sits inside the company's 0.9–1.25x target range. Leverage still amplifies credit losses — that risk is carried in the bear/super-bear multipliers (0.90/0.75), not in this ratio.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear C at 11.46% vs bull B at 18.68%): accepted — the verdict is sized to the bear end: bear IV@15% $13.72 sits ~27% below the $18.72 price.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range, and it is unusually wide because the template barely fits a BDC: the engine-native OCF base prints a mechanical Tier F; the net-income base actually used (3-yr median $2.4391/share) gives Tier C at 14.46% weighted IRR; the same scenario set on the latest-FY net-income base ($1.8584/share, diagnostic run, same inputs) gives Tier C at 11.58% weighted IRR and IV@15% $13.66. Every defensible reading lands in C-or-worse at $18.72 — the disagreement is only about how far below the hurdle it sits.
- What the DCF cannot see is what BDC buyers actually underwrite: NAV and dividend coverage. On those, ARCC at $18.72 trades at a ~3% discount to Q2 2026 NAV of $19.35 with a $1.92 dividend covered by FY2025 NII of $2.02/share but **not** covered by Q2 2026 core EPS ($0.47 vs $0.48) for a second consecutive quarter — the spillover buffer (~$1.38/share) is what bridges that gap, and it is finite.
- Watch items: non-accrual trend (2.4% at cost at Q2 2026, up from 1.8% at FY2025), PIK share of income, whether core EPS re-covers the dividend, and NAV/share direction. Q3 2026 results are scheduled for October 27, 2026.
- Margin of safety: none on the weighted case — IV@15% $17.93 is 4.2% **below** the price. A buyer at $18.72 is paid if the base case (flat per-share earnings on the normalized base) holds, and is exposed to the bear case ($13.72) if credit turns.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: C** (weighted IRR 14.46% on the corrected net-income base; method range F on the rejected OCF template to C on any net-income base)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector model misfit; base is a judgment override; per-share earnings trend is falling)
- One-liner: Largest BDC on the Ares direct-lending platform, moat 5/10 — the engine's OCF base is a sector artifact (loan purchases are operating outflows; OCF-based OE was negative in 4 of the last 5 years despite a covered $1.92/share dividend); on the corrected net-income base of $2.44/share the $18.72 price yields a 14.46% weighted IRR (Tier C) with weighted IV@15% of $17.93 — just short of the 15% hurdle, clearing it only at or below ~$17.93 and sized to the bear end (IV@15% $13.72) not at all; the finance-sector model misfit and a falling per-share earnings trend (TTM net income $960M through Q2 2026 vs $1,299M in FY2025, fundamentals.json) cap confidence at low.
